LESSON: READING 11.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: NON- FICTION

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.2: Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non- fiction

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non- fiction. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: what he or she has read about. 1. What is the importance of reading widely?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify print and non- print non-fiction materials that are interesting to read
2. read a range of non- fiction materials for general information
3. appreciate the importance of reading for information

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 11.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: NON- FICTION
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non- fiction helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 11.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: NON- FICTION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify print and non- print non-fiction materials that are interesting to read

What this means
In this part you learn to identify print and non- print non-fiction materials that are interesting to read. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify print and non- print non-fiction materials that are interesting to read.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non- fiction”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify print and non- print non-fiction materials that are interesting to read. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Read a range of non- fiction materials for general information

What this means
In this part you learn to read a range of non- fiction materials for general information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read a range of non- fiction materials for general information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non- fiction to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read a range of non- fiction materials for general information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the importance of reading for information

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of reading for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of reading for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of reading for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non- fiction is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non- fiction”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify print and non- print non-fiction materials that are interesting to read)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non- fiction to a partner. (skill: read a range of non- fiction materials for general information)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the importance of reading for information)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non- fiction to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify print and non- print non-fiction materials that are interesting to read.
3. Practise this skill: read a range of non- fiction materials for general information.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the importance of reading for information.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non- fiction from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non- fiction: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non- fiction?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. what he or she has read about. 1. What is the importance of reading widely?
2. What do you consider when selecting a reading text?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Reading: Non- fiction means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify print and non- print non-fiction materials that are interesting to read.
5. Be able to: read a range of non- fiction materials for general information.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
